what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat diarrhea. Difenoxin works by slowing down the movement of your intestines, which helps your stool become more solid and reduces how often you need to go to the bathroom. Atropine is added in a very small amount to help prevent misuse of this medication.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not take more than the prescribed amount, as this medicine can be habit-forming. Only take it for as long as your doctor tells you to.
dosing: For adults, the usual starting dose is 2 tablets (each tablet contains 1 mg difenoxin and 0.025 mg atropine) taken at first, then 1 tablet after each loose stool or every 3 to 4 hours as needed. Do not take more than 8 tablets in one day. Your doctor will tell you the exact dose that is right for you. This medicine is NOT recommended for children under 2 years of age.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C and 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine in a safe place, tightly closed, and out of the reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase dizziness and drowsiness. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything requiring alertness until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medicines that cause drowsiness, such as sleeping pills, anxiety medicines, or other pain medicines, unless your doctor approves. Tell your doctor about all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you are taking before starting this medication.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: diarrhea that lasts more than 2 days or gets worse; stomach pain or bloating that is severe or new; fever or blood in your stool; signs of dehydration such as dry mouth, dizziness, or very little urination; slow or difficult breathing; extreme drowsiness or difficulty waking up; fast or pounding heartbeat; flushing or warmth of the skin; difficulty swallowing or dry mouth that is severe; or any signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing.
when_it_works: This medicine usually starts working within 45 minutes to 1 hour after taking it. Most people notice fewer trips to the bathroom and firmer stools within a few hours. If your diarrhea does not improve within 48 hours, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine, especially dizziness and drowsiness, which can increase the risk of falls. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it may not be safe during pregnancy. Breastfeeding: This medicine may pass into breast milk and could affect your baby. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medication. Liver or kidney disease: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney problems, as dose adjustments may be needed. Children: This medicine should NOT be used in children under 2 years of age. Use with extreme caution in young children, as accidental overdose can be very dangerous.
